verdict: Yes, if you sell genuine handwork and prove it. Lucknow Chikankari has a GI tag and a large artisan base, and buyers pay a real premium for hand-embroidered pieces. The traps are machine-made imitations undercutting you on price, high returns for size and fit, and slow production, so the brands that last start made-to-order.
angle: Lucknow's Chikankari cluster employs a very large number of artisans, many of them women embroidering at home through middlemen. That supply chain makes it easy to buy pieces but hard to guarantee authenticity or fair pay. A brand that works directly with artisan groups, shows each maker and the hours in each piece, and uses modern silhouettes for younger buyers stands out from both cheap imitations and traditional stores.

faq.q: How much does it cost to start a Chikankari clothing brand?
faq.a: A made-to-order launch with 30–60 pieces, a photoshoot and a website costs ₹1–3 lakh. KidharMilega's Lucknow ODOP data puts a larger setup at ₹1.5–50 lakh.

faq.q: How can buyers tell real Chikankari from machine embroidery?
faq.a: Hand embroidery has slight irregularities and knots on the reverse, while machine work is perfectly uniform. Brands build trust by showing close-ups, the artisan and the time each piece took.

faq.q: What margin does a Chikankari brand make?
faq.a: District data shows 20–30% gross margin selling wholesale and 50–65% selling direct. Returns and marketing reduce what you keep, so control sizing carefully.
